You're not trying to bulk. At all.

Which is more important to you? Shredding fat or building muscle?

Also, 20 minutes of cardio is just barely enough time to get your body into fat-burning mode. If you're eating such a low number of calories, you're gonna drop muscle and bone weight as well as fat if you don't stress your muscles/bones. I'd recommend adding some bodyweight resistance cardio, unless you're going for like... a distance runner's build.

Replace your cardio with sprints, or better yet sprints up hills.

You have to lift to make gains.

What do you want to look like? Because right now your training like a long distance runner would. Not a good one mind you, but that's your training. You are your training.

If you want to get jacked start doing football work outs that focus on explosion and power. Bench, squats, dead lifts, curls, shrugs, push ups, pull ups, burpees, etc.

This is a bit overly simplified, but I think it might help.

  1. Cardio burns calories in the moment. Muscle burns calories all day. Add weight training.

  2. You can't 'cut' and gain at the same time. But, you can lose weight while building strength. Try looking into 'lean gains', it's a longer process, but sounds more like what you're trying to accomplish.

  3. Don't believe calorie burn on machines. My personal experience is that they are typically half of what you think.

  4. @Datawych is correct. 20 min, is not going to get you into the fat burn zone. I'm assuming you're cranking the resistance for a muscle burn, if you're going for cardio burn try @Mercuenomia or @JamesGatz suggestions.

  5. Personally, I would never drop core work. Your core is your stability, it's going to give you better posture, and generally give all your other exercises better technique.
